answer: An oasis compute market requires each rewarded identity to solve a verifiable delay puzzle. At the zenith of each round, a fresh public beacon fixes the challenge from the round and public key; the verification kernel checks both the delay proof and that binding. Copying one proof across aliases fails. Under a sound sequential-work assumption, n identities require roughly n times the processor work, even if a farm buys parallel machines. This prices extra claims in computation instead of usernames. It assumes unshortcuttable puzzles and offers no protection against wealthy compute owners.
